extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians applying for academic/faculty/editorial positions or AMS membership (job-seekers, prospective editors, and prospective members)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural requirements for applying to faculty chairs/lectureships and an editorial appointment in mathematics (materials required, desired qualifications, deadlines, and other selection preferences). Also includes AMS membership classification rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference letters requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrange to have at least four letters of reference sent directly to Professor K. Murty, Associate Chair, Department of Mathematics, University of Toronto. At least one letter should be primarily concerned with the candidate's teaching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters must be sent directly (not via applicant). To ensure full consideration these should be received by December 31, 1992 (as stated for that posting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research-area fit for Sussex lectureship
rubrics_metrics.description: The appointee is expected to have research interests in the general area of Algebra/Topology/Geometry and interact with existing faculty in these fields; outstanding candidates with research interests in Analysis, Statistics or Applied Mathematics already represented at Sussex should also apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates should indicate how their research complements/ interacts with existing faculty; completed application forms available from Personnel Office and must be returned by 23 October 1992.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completed application form / deadline (Sussex)
rubrics_metrics.description: Further particulars and application forms may be obtained ... Completed forms should be returned by 23 October 1992.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the institution's instructions for forms and meet the posted deadline to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associate Editor (Mathematical Reviews) — breadth and subject preference
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual with considerable breadth in pure or applied mathematics is sought and preference will be given those applicants with expertise in numerical analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should demonstrate broad knowledge across mathematics; explicit evidence of expertise in numerical analysis is advantageous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associate Editor — essential language/writing skills
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability to write good English is essential and the ability to read mathematics in major foreign languages is important. (The ability to read mathematical articles in Russian or Chinese is especially desirable.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples of clear English writing (publications, edited work) and indicate foreign language reading ability where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associate Editor — job responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsibilities include selecting articles and books suitable for review, classifying these items, assigning them to reviewers, editing the reviews when they are returned, and correcting the galley proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should demonstrate editorial experience or skills relevant to these tasks; be prepared to perform day-to-day editorial operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associate Editor — application materials and references
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications (including curriculum vitae, bibliography, and names and addresses of at least three references) should be sent to Dr. D. G. Babbitt, Executive Editor, Mathematical Reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full CV, bibliography, and contact information for ≥3 referees; follow the contact method (postal/email/fax) given in the posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and practical constraint (NSA recruiting ad)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should be mathematicians capable of contributing to cryptologic problems using Number Theory, Group Theory, Finite Field Theory, Linear Algebra, Probability Theory, Mathematical Statistics, Combinatorics and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resume should highlight problem-solving experience in these areas; note that U.S. citizenship is required for applicants and immediate family members for NSA positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chair (University of Auckland) — outstanding record and contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: The successful applicant will have an outstanding academic and research background in some branch of Pure Mathematics with personal qualities and experience which will enable her/him to contribute significantly to the continuing development of Pure Mathematics at Auckland both in research and teaching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should demonstrate outstanding research and teaching accomplishments; include requested number of copies (three) and meet the specified closing date (20 November 1992); quote vacancy number UAC.197.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kerr Chair (Oklahoma State) — scholarly accomplishments and research commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates should have an outstanding record of scholarly accomplishments and a strong commitment to research. The person selected will be expected to maintain a strong research program and be actively involved in the development of the department, including the graduate and undergraduate programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit vita and names/addresses of references; applications should be received by the full-consideration deadline (November 1, 1992). Salary and other terms negotiable; women and minorities encouraged to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professor of Pure Mathematics (Massey) — distinguished research and teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should be distinguished in research in one or more fields of Pure Mathematics and have proven ability in teaching. The appointee will be expected to provide direction within the Department, University, and in the wider community and may be expected to serve a term as Head of Department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should include full curriculum vitae and names, addresses and fax numbers of three referees; quote reference number NAMS 54/92 and meet the closing date (31 October 1992).

rubrics_metrics.name: National University of Singapore — degree and teaching/research expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are invited ... from candidates who must possess a relevant PhD degree. Preference will be given to those who are able to teach in more than one of the areas listed under the discipline they are applying to and with proven ability in research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State teaching versatility and evidence of research; for Computational Mathematics, specialization in geometric modelling or statistical computing and experience with UNIX graphics workstations is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position-specific technical/experience requirements (NUS computational programme)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computational Mathematics — Applicants should specialize in either geometric modelling or statistical computing. Experience with UNIX graphics workstations is essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include details of specialization and practical experience with UNIX graphics workstations in application materials; visiting appointments for one or two years also considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application procedural instructions (various postings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many postings require specific documents (CV/vita, bibliographies, names/addresses of referees), specific numbers of copies, quoting of vacancy/reference numbers, and returning materials to named addresses or contacts by stated deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully follow each posting's submission instructions (recipient, number of copies, quote vacancy number, fax/email where provided) and meet the listed deadline to ensure full consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMS membership category — income and verification rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Membership categories and dues depend on annual professional income (below $45,000 dues $81; $45,000 or more dues $108); CMS Cooperative Rate for certain members outside U.S.; students or unemployed dues are $27 and annual verification is required; reciprocity membership rules and dues for those outside U.S. and Canada are specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select appropriate membership category based on income and residency; provide verification where required; joint family membership has special dues treatment and mailing privileges rules.
